question.problem:
Calculate $\text{Cov}(x,y)$ for the following data sets:

$$
x=\{-4,\,2,\,6,\,8\},\,y=\{2,\,-9,\,3,\,12\}
$$
question.worked_solution:
The (population) covariance of the data sets $x=\{{x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}\}$ and $y=\{{y}_{1},{y}_{2},…,{y}_{n}\}$ is given by 

$$
\text{Cov}(x,y)=\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}({x}_{i}-\overset{―}{x})({y}_{i}-\overset{―}{y}),
$$

where $\overset{―}{x}=\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}$ and $\overset{―}{y}=\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{y}_{i}$ are the means of the data sets.

First, we need to compute the means:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{x} & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot ((-4)+2+6+8) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot 12 \\  & =3 \\ \overset{―}{y} & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{y}_{i} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot (2+(-9)+3+12) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot 8 \\  & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the covariance of our data sets is

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Cov}(x,y) & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}({x}_{i}-\overset{―}{x})({y}_{i}-\overset{―}{y}) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[(-4-3)(2-2)+(2-3)(-9-2)+(6-3)(3-2)+(8-3)(12-2)] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[(-7)(0)+(-1)(-11)+(3)(1)+(5)(10)] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[0+11+3+50] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot 64 \\  & =16.\end{aligned}
$$
